caption:
OpenAI just launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its AI agents, called dots, pay for things you want to buy.
The agent never sees your real card number: Visa, Mastercard and American Express hand it a payment token instead.
You still approve every purchase with Face ID or a fingerprint. For now it is only for US ChatGPT Pro users 18 and older.

Would you let an AI agent shop with your credit card?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 9to5Mac
threads_text: ChatGPT can now pay for things. OpenAI's new Wallet lets its dots agents check out with a token from Visa, Mastercard or Amex, and you approve each order with Face ID. Only US Pro users for now, and stores that block agents will not work. Would you hand an AI agent your credit card?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, 2026, a payment feature that lets its dots agents complete purchases for users. According to 9to5Mac, OpenAI describes it as the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to a user's actual card details, and it requires a security check for every purchase.

The wallet was built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and cards from all three networks work at launch, according to SQ Magazine. A user adds an eligible card once and can then let a dot use it at checkout.

Before each purchase, the user sees a review screen with the items, the total and the card that will be charged. The user then approves with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval also creates a record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.

At payment, the card network issues a payment token that stands in for the card. The token carries its own card number, security code and expiration date, so the charge lands on the selected card while neither the merchant nor the agent receives the real card details. The dot passes the shipping address and contact information to the merchant.

OpenAI says existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes still apply. Data Studios reports that merchants may not save or reuse the token for a separate purchase, that recurring billing is allowed only with customer consent where the checkout supports it, and that at launch a dot cannot buy anything without the user's approval.

The first rollout is limited to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States who are 18 or older and hold an eligible US-issued card. OpenAI has not given a date for a wider rollout or named other countries. According to 9to5Mac, the company says the limited launch lets it learn from real use and work with businesses, banks and payment networks on compatibility and reliability.
Dots are the always-on agents OpenAI introduced on September 29, 2026. Data Studios reports that each dot has its own cloud computer and browser and connects to more than 4,000 apps through plugins.

The wallet will not work on websites that block AI agents, which 9to5Mac describes as a growing problem online. SQ Magazine notes that Amazon has banned outside agents and steers shoppers to its own assistant, Alexa. OpenAI offers a Commerce Partner Playbook for merchants that want to serve agent shoppers.

According to Data Studios, the wallet works with existing checkout pages without a dedicated integration, and OpenAI is sending signals such as IP address, country and locale so merchants can run fraud checks, working with companies including Stripe, Adyen, Checkout.com, Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd. The same report says OpenAI takes no cut of purchases for now.
OpenAI plans to add spending limits, category rules and time windows that would let users pre-approve some purchases, but it has not given a date for those controls.

The design keeps a person in the loop for every order at launch, which limits how much an agent can do on its own but also limits the damage from a mistake. The bigger test is outside OpenAI's control: whether retailers let agents through their checkouts or keep blocking them in favor of their own assistants.
Watch whether the planned spending limits and pre-approved purchases arrive, since that would be the first time ChatGPT agents could spend money without a fresh approval for each order.
